## Natural history notes

A slender native snake characterized by a bright green back, pale yellow to whitish underside, large eyes, and strongly keeled scales that give the body a slightly rough texture. Rough Greensnakes occur throughout Florida in shrubs, vines, forest edges, wetlands, hammocks, and vegetation bordering ponds, streams, and marshes. They are highly arboreal and spend much of their time moving slowly through branches and foliage, where their coloration provides excellent camouflage. They feed primarily on insects and spiders, including caterpillars, grasshoppers, crickets, and other small arthropods, and are harmless to people.
